prerequisites: Mathematics knowledge (especially vector and matrix calculus)

learning_outcomes.text: Students will have a basic knowledge of image data representation, know the procedure for extracting information, and know fundamental image processing algorithms as well as the basics of Artificial Neural Networks for image recognition.
Students deepen their programming skills and know the steps of image processing from pixel representation to the extraction of knowledge from images using selected algorithms and methods.
After successful completion of this module, students can implement image processing algorithms and solve simple classification tasks using Artificial Neural Networks.

syllabus_topics: Image processing – point operations, filters (linear/nonlinear), geometric transformations
Object extraction and representation in binary images
Fundamentals of Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) – Deep NN, Convolutional NN, datasets
Features for object recognition (classical BV and ANN)
Object and image classification (classical and with ANN)
assessment_rules: The graded assessment is either a written project report (approx. 10-15 pages with a 20-minute explanation) or an oral examination (details as per the General Examination Regulations). The ungraded assessment is experimental work, consisting of approximately 5 experiments in total.
